emergency.general: Dial 999 for police, ambulance, and fire emergencies. English is an official language and widely understood by emergency operators. Outside Nairobi and major cities, emergency response times may be longer — the Kenya Tourism Federation Safety and Communication Center also provides tourist assistance.

healthcare.summary: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Kenya. Emergency numbers (999), yellow fever vaccination required, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, malaria precautions, and travel insurance advice.

medications.prescriptionRules: A prescription is required for prescription medications but enforcement varies. Antibiotics and many drugs available OTC. Carry all medications in original packaging with a doctor's note.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD stimulant medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Stimulants are controlled substances. Bring original prescription, doctor's letter, and only the amount needed. Declare at customs.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is controlled. Carry alternatives if possible.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications (diazepam, alprazolam, etc.)
restrictedMeds.note: Benzodiazepines require documentation. Carry a doctor's letter explaining medical necessity.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotics (morphine, tramadol, etc.)
restrictedMeds.note: Strong narcotics require strict documentation. Carry alternatives or minimal quantities with documentation.

medications.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. For controlled substances, carry original prescriptions and a note explaining medical necessity. Yellow fever certificate required for entry from endemic countries.
medications.generalAdvice: Kenya imposes severe penalties for drug offences — up to 10 years for possession and life imprisonment for trafficking. Carry all prescription medications in original packaging with a valid prescription and doctor's letter. Declare controlled substances at customs upon arrival.

controlledSubstances.note: Part II of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act; prescription required. Carry doctor's letter for import
Amphetamines are prohibited under Kenya's NDPS Act; Adderall is not available and importation is illegal
Cannabis (bhang) is illegal under NDPS Act despite cultural use; CBD products are also prohibited
Controlled psychotropic substance; available by prescription in Kenya. Travelers should carry prescription documentation
Codeine is controlled; available in low-dose OTC cough syrups but pure codeine needs prescription. Carry documentation for import
Controlled precursor chemical under Kenyan law; pharmacy-only sale. Travelers should carry original packaging
Illegal under NDPS Act; trafficking carries penalties up to life imprisonment or death (though death penalty rarely enforced)
Prescription controlled substance; increasingly regulated due to abuse concerns. Carry prescription and doctor's letter
Prescription required; importable with valid documentation for personal use

scams.name: Safari Price Gouging
scams.description: Unlicensed operators offer cheap safaris then demand extra fees or provide substandard vehicles.
scams.avoidance: Book with KATO-registered operators. Get full pricing in writing.

scams.name: Matatu Pickpocketing
scams.description: Pickpockets operate on crowded matatus, especially CBD routes.
scams.avoidance: Keep valuables in front pockets. Use ride-sharing apps for longer trips.

scams.name: Fake M-Pesa Agents
scams.description: Scammers pose as M-Pesa agents asking for test payments or your PIN.
scams.avoidance: Only use official Safaricom shops. Never share your PIN.

connectivity.simOptions: Safaricom (M-Pesa network) prepaid SIM at JKIA airport or any Safaricom shop. Need passport. Data is cheap. M-Pesa mobile money is essential.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Good WiFi at hotels and cafes in Nairobi and Mombasa. Limited in safari parks and rural areas. Some lodges have WiFi.
connectivity.bestOption: Safaricom prepaid SIM — essential for M-Pesa mobile payments (widely used for everything). Buy at airport on arrival.

cultural.tipping: 10% at restaurants. Safari guides/drivers: $15-25/day per person. Hotel porters: KES 200-500.
cultural.dressCode: Modest dress in rural and coastal areas (Muslim regions). Safari: neutral colors. Nairobi is more cosmopolitan and casual.
cultural.greetings: 'Jambo' or 'Habari yako' (how are you). Handshake is standard. Elders and authority figures addressed with respect.
taboos: Photographing people without asking (especially Maasai — negotiate a fee)
Pointing at wildlife during safari (use open hand)
Disrespecting the flag or national symbols
cultural.haggling: Expected at markets, souvenir shops, matatus (minibuses), and with taxi drivers. Not at supermarkets. Start at 40-50% of asking price.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: e-Visa required ($50). Apply online before travel. Some nationalities eligible for visa on arrival. ETA system being implemented.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: January-March (hot, dry — good for safari). July-October (Great Migration in Masai Mara). June-October dry season overall best.

stalenessWarnings.message: Some data in this profile may be outdated. Connect to the internet to refresh.

steps: File a police report immediately — get the report number, you will need it
Contact the US Embassy or nearest consulate: Contact the nearest US Embassy
Bring the police report + any ID you have (driver's license, copy of passport)
Apply for an Emergency Passport (usually issued within 1-2 business days)
Notify your travel insurance and airline of the situation
stolenPassport.notes: Keep a digital copy of your passport in cloud storage (Google Photos, iCloud) and email yourself a scan before travel.

steps: Go to the nearest police station (or call 999)
Bring ID or a copy of your passport if available
Request a written report — ask for an English copy or certified translation if needed
Keep the report number safe — required for insurance claims
For theft: list all stolen items with approximate values
policeReport.notes: In many countries, tourist police stations are available in major cities — they have English-speaking staff. Ask your hotel concierge for the nearest tourist police.

steps: If involved in an accident: do not move vehicles if anyone is injured
Call police (999) and ambulance (999) if there are injuries
Exchange contact, license, and insurance details with other parties
Document the scene with photos before moving vehicles
Contact your rental car company's emergency line
Contact your travel insurance's 24h assistance line
roadsideAssistance.notes: Traffic drives on the LEFT. An International Driving Permit (IDP) is required for most foreign licenses. Rental vehicles are available at major airports and cities.

immediate: Avoid river banks and low-lying areas during heavy rain
Do not attempt to cross flooded roads on foot or by vehicle
Move to higher ground if in flood-prone area
Follow Kenya Red Cross and local authority alerts
after: Avoid contact with floodwater — leptospirosis and cholera risk
Boil or purify drinking water after floods
